lines:
User turns now survive compaction verbatim instead of existing only as summary prose.

What changed
- New CHECKPOINT_PREAMBLE constant and is_checkpoint() in compaction/mod.rs; frame_summary uses the constant. The preamble doubles as the marker that distinguishes a prior checkpoint from a real user turn.
- New pinned_user_units(surface, cut) in surface.rs: real user-role messages from the shadowed span (no instruction_event_id, not a checkpoint) are carried across the boundary. The first user turn is kept unconditionally; later ones are kept newest-first while pinning still costs at most half of what the span frees, so a pasted specification cannot defeat the reduction. Units keep their original relative order, so the provider prefix survives to the first dropped unit.
- runtime.rs builds the replacement from the pinned units plus the checkpoint plus the retained tail, with a fallback: if carrying the user turns cannot shrink the span (one oversized direction and little else), the plain summary+tail replacement is used so compaction still makes progress. The shrink check now compares the whole replacement against the shadowed span, and context.compacted records pinnedUnits and pinnedTokenCount.

Divergence from the task text worth recording: the task said a user message may only enter the shadowed range when nothing else is left, and the first prompt is pinned unconditionally. Unconditional pinning of a first turn that dominates the span makes any compaction unable to reduce, which the existing history() fixture exposed (a ~25k-token first turn against a 16k window). The implemented rule keeps the first turn unconditional whenever it still permits a reduction and otherwise falls back to the plain replacement. That preserves the invariant that a committed compaction always reduces, at the cost of summarising (never deleting without summary) a pathological oversized first turn.

Verification
- Unit tests in compaction/tests.rs: user turns pinned in original order; an oversized late user turn cannot defeat the reduction; a prior checkpoint and instruction messages are not pinned as user turns.
- Integration tests through the real authority: a_compaction_keeps_the_user_direction_and_consolidates_prior_checkpoints asserts the first prompt survives verbatim and pinnedUnits/pinnedTokenCount are recorded; a_compaction_replaces_a_prior_checkpoint_instead_of_pinning_it asserts exactly one checkpoint remains after a surface that already carried one.
- Full desktop suite: 462 passed, 1 ignored, 0 failed. capability-host unaffected.

One flake observed: successive_actual_compactions_rearm_missing_scopes_and_preserve_partial_survival failed once in a parallel run and then passed 8 consecutive runs (3 alone, 5 with the full compaction_integration filter). The same test flaked once during task 132 before this change; it is order/parallelism dependent, not caused by pinning.

Compaction shadows the leading span with no regard for message role, so the user's direction can be summarised away while bulk tool output is judged on token count alone.

Current behaviour (desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/compaction/surface.rs): `select_prefix` walks backwards accumulating `Unit::tokens()` and returns a cut; `Unit::tokens` prices a user message exactly like a tool exchange. `replace_units` keeps only the first ordinary user message as the request base, so everything before the cut — including the original first prompt — is replaced by the checkpoint.

Measured evidence (chat.3fdeab43b37ed6406ff6a62b53fa01bec2a3ca30, test1_qwen, one compaction): the first request after compaction has input.messages = [system 13,425 chars, checkpoint summary 20,706 chars], one clock context message and 44 retained exchanges. The original prompt text ("self-contained Tetris clone") appears only inside the summary prose, in no verbatim message. DSH behaves identically because the first prompt is inside the shadowed range.

Precedent to copy: Hermes protects the first 3 and last 20 messages by count (`protect_first_n=3`, `protect_last_n=20` in agent/context_compressor.py) on top of its 20% tail; Codex rebuilds the replacement history as every user message up to COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS = 20,000 tokens plus the summary (codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs, build_compacted_history).

Change: make user-role messages unshadowable while any assistant/tool unit remains, and pin the first user message unconditionally. A user message may only enter the shadowed range when nothing else is left, and the cut must stay a balanced boundary. Keep the pinned messages at their original positions so the provider prefix stays stable.

Tests: the first prompt survives repeated compactions byte-for-byte; a large tool result before a user message is shadowed first; the checkpoint summary never becomes the only copy of the prompt; existing balanced-boundary, shrink and prefix-stability tests are unchanged; a pinned head does not break cache-prefix accounting.

data.title: Pin user messages, and the first prompt in particular, outside the compacted prefix
